item.title: How to find safe Minecraft mods (and avoid fake ones)
item.description: Download Minecraft mods safely: use trusted platforms like Modrinth, check the loader and version, read the page, and avoid .exe files and random links.
item.content:encoded:
Most Minecraft mods are made by hobbyists in good faith, but fake download pages and bad files do exist. This checklist helps you pick mods that are safer and more likely to work.

1. Use a trusted platform

Download from a well-known mod platform such as Modrinth rather than a random link from a video description, a chat message or a file-sharing site. The mod manager in FireClient can browse Modrinth directly.

2. Remember what a mod file looks like

A Fabric mod is a .jar file that goes in your mods folder. A mod is not an installer. If something calls itself a mod but you have to run an .exe, a .bat or a .msi, do not run it.

3. Check version and loader

Open the Versions tab and filter for Minecraft 1.21.1 and Fabric. The mods guide shows how. A wrong version is the most common reason for a crash.

4. Read the project page

Look for a clear description, a source code link, an issue tracker, recent updates and a reasonable number of downloads. A page with no description, copied text or only a download button is a warning sign.

5. Check the dependencies

Many mods need Fabric API or another mod. Install only the required ones the page lists.

6. Be careful with unknown authors

For a new or unknown author, read comments and issues and start with well-known mods first.

7. Test and keep a backup

Add one mod at a time and back up your worlds before big changes. If the game crashes, use the crash checklist.

If something looks wrong

If you ran a file you now doubt, run a scan with Windows Security, change your Microsoft account password and review your account activity. Never share access tokens or account files with anyone.

item.title: Best Minecraft settings for PvP on 1.21.1 (Java Edition)
item.description: Set up Minecraft 1.21.1 for PvP: stable FPS, raw mouse input, sensible distances, a clean HUD with FPS and coordinates, and respect for server rules.
item.content:encoded:
Good PvP comes down to steady frames, predictable mouse input and a screen that shows what you need. These settings are a starting point for Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.1. Adjust them to your PC and your taste.

1. Aim for steady frames

A high, stable frame rate helps more than a high peak. Lower render distance to around 8 to 12 chunks, turn off fancy graphics and reduce particles. The FPS guide covers memory, Java 21 and Fabric performance mods.

2. Use raw mouse input

In Options, Controls, Mouse Settings, turn on Raw Input so the game reads your mouse directly. Then set sensitivity to something you can repeat, and keep it the same across sessions.

3. Pick a comfortable field of view

A wider FOV shows more of the fight, and a narrower one makes targets larger. Test a few values and keep the one you aim best with.

4. Limit visual noise

Turn off clouds, lower biome blend and keep particles minimal, so fast action is easy to read.

5. Build a clean HUD

Show only what you use. FPS and coordinates are common choices, and too many elements crowd the screen. In FireClient you can drag each HUD element where you want it and keep the rest off. Back up your layout once you are happy.

6. Check your connection and PC

Close background apps, use a wired connection if you can and check your ping on the server you play on.

7. Follow the server's rules

Some servers restrict certain client features or mods. Read the rules before you join and use only what is allowed. No setting replaces practice, and these changes just remove avoidable obstacles.

item.title: Minecraft launcher not opening on Windows? Try these fixes
item.description: A Minecraft launcher that will not open on Windows 10 or 11 is usually blocked, stuck or damaged. Work through these safe fixes, including SmartScreen and reinstalling.
item.content:encoded:
If a launcher does nothing when you open it, the cause is usually a stuck process, a blocked file or a damaged install. These steps are safe to try in order, and they apply to most Windows launchers, including FireClient.

1. Restart and try again

Close the launcher, restart your PC and open it once. A leftover background process from an earlier crash is a common cause.

2. End a stuck process

Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager. If you see the launcher listed, right-click it and choose End task, then open it again.

3. Check that the file is not blocked

Right-click the installer or the launcher file, choose Properties and look for an Unblock checkbox near the bottom of the General tab. Tick it and press OK. Only do this for a file you downloaded from an official source, and verify it first with the steps in the safety guide.

4. Look at SmartScreen and antivirus

Windows SmartScreen or your antivirus can stop an unsigned installer from running. The FireClient early access installer is unsigned, so a prompt is expected. If you have verified the SHA-256 and downloaded from the official page, you can choose to run it. If you are not sure, do not run it.

5. Check your system

FireClient needs Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit). Make sure Windows is up to date and you have free disk space.

6. Reinstall cleanly

Uninstall the launcher in Windows Settings, restart, download a fresh copy from the official download page and install again. Your worlds are not stored in the installer folder, but back up your worlds first to be safe.

7. Ask for help

If it still fails, ask in the FireClient Discord. Say your Windows version and what happens when you click. Never post account files or access tokens.

item.title: What is a Minecraft client? Launcher, Fabric and mods explained
item.description: Minecraft launcher, client, mod loader and mod: what each term means, how Fabric fits in, and how FireClient combines a launcher with a Fabric client.
item.content:encoded:
People use "launcher", "client" and "mod" as if they mean the same thing. They do not. Here is what each one is, and how they fit together.

Launcher

A launcher is the program that signs you in, picks a game version and starts Minecraft. It also manages profiles, memory settings and game files. The standard Minecraft Launcher is one example, and FireClient includes a launcher too.

Mod loader

A mod loader is software that lets Minecraft load mods. Fabric is a lightweight mod loader that is popular for fast updates to new Minecraft versions. Other loaders include Forge, NeoForge and Quilt. A mod must be built for the loader you use.

Mod

A mod is a file that changes or adds something to the game, such as better performance or a new interface. Mods are usually shared on sites like Modrinth. See the mods guide for how to pick the right file.

Client

A client is a package of features that runs inside the game, often for quality-of-life and display tweaks. Examples include a customisable HUD with FPS, coordinates and other readouts, or a menu to switch settings. A client is built on top of a mod loader.

How FireClient fits

FireClient combines a launcher with a Fabric client. The launcher starts Minecraft Java Edition on Windows, and the in-game client adds a draggable HUD and a menu that opens with Right Shift, for Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric with Java 21. Set up the HUD in the HUD guide.

One more thing

Some servers have rules about which client features are allowed. Read a server's rules before you join, and respect them.

item.title: How to back up your Minecraft worlds on Windows
item.description: Back up Minecraft Java worlds before updates or mods: find the saves folder, copy the world while the game is closed, zip it with a date and restore it later.
item.content:encoded:
A world can be lost to a bad mod, a crash or a mistake. A two-minute backup protects hours of building. This guide covers Minecraft Java Edition on Windows.

1. Close the game

Quit Minecraft completely so no files are being written. Copying a world while the game is open can produce a damaged backup.

2. Find your saves folder

In the standard Minecraft setup, worlds are in %appdata%\.minecraft\saves. Paste that into the File Explorer address bar and press Enter. Each folder inside is one world. A launcher that uses a different game folder will show its own saves folder, so check your launcher's settings. The worlds library in FireClient lists your worlds with an icon, save date and size, which helps you pick the right one.

3. Copy the world

Right-click the world folder, choose copy, and paste it somewhere else, such as Documents. For a smaller file, right-click the copy and choose Send to, Compressed (zipped) folder.

4. Name it with the date

Rename the backup with the world name and date, for example Survival-2026-10-17. Keep a few older copies, not only the latest one.

5. Keep one copy off your PC

Put a copy on an external drive or in cloud storage, so a dead drive does not take both copies.

When to back up

  • Before installing or removing mods
  • Before updating Minecraft or changing the Fabric version
  • Before testing a large build or redstone project

How to restore

Close the game, delete or rename the broken world folder in saves, then paste your backup folder in its place. Open the game and the world appears in the list.

For settings rather than worlds, see how to back up your FireClient HUD layout.

item.title: How to install Java 21 for Minecraft 1.21.1 on Windows
item.description: Minecraft 1.21.1 needs Java 21. Check your Java version, install a trusted Java 21 build on Windows 10 or 11, and fix common Java errors.
item.content:encoded:
Minecraft 1.21.1 runs on Java 21. Older Java versions can stop the game from starting. This guide shows how to check what you have and install the right one on Windows 10 or 11.

1. Check your current Java version

Press the Windows key, type cmd and open Command Prompt. Type java -version and press Enter. If the first line shows a version that starts with 21, you are ready. If it shows 8, 11 or 17, or says Java is not recognised, continue.

2. Download Java 21

Download a Java 21 build for Windows x64 from a trusted vendor. Eclipse Temurin and the Microsoft Build of OpenJDK are common choices. Pick the JDK or JRE 21 installer (.msi) and avoid unknown download sites.

3. Install it

Run the installer. If it offers options such as adding Java to PATH or setting JAVA_HOME, enable them. Finish the install.

4. Check again

Close Command Prompt, open a new one and run java -version. It should now show version 21.

5. Restart your launcher

Close and reopen your launcher so it picks up the new Java. In FireClient, start the Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric profile and check that it opens.

Common problems

  • Still shows an old version. Another Java install is earlier in your PATH. Uninstall the old one in Windows Settings, then check again.
  • "Java not found". Reinstall and make sure the PATH option was enabled.
  • Game still crashes. Follow the crash checklist.

Always download installers from the vendor's official site and never from a video description or file-sharing link. The safety guide explains how to verify a file with SHA-256.

item.title: How to fix Minecraft crashing on launch (Fabric 1.21.1)
item.description: Minecraft 1.21.1 crashes on launch with Fabric? Work through this checklist: Java 21, mod versions, Fabric API, memory, drivers and how to read the crash report.
item.content:encoded:
If Minecraft 1.21.1 closes right after you press Play, work through this list in order. Most Fabric crashes come from a mismatched mod, the wrong Java version or a missing dependency.

1. Check your Java version

Minecraft 1.21.1 needs Java 21. Open Command Prompt and type java -version. If it shows an older version, follow the Java 21 guide.

2. Remove the last mod you added

Move the newest mod out of your mods folder and launch again. If the game starts, that mod was the cause. Look for a newer file that supports 1.21.1.

3. Check every mod's version and loader

Each mod must list Minecraft 1.21.1 and Fabric. Files for Forge, NeoForge, Quilt or a different Minecraft version will not load. The Modrinth mods guide shows how to filter for the right file.

4. Make sure Fabric API is installed

Many mods need Fabric API. If a crash report says a dependency is missing, install the version that matches 1.21.1.

5. Test with no mods

Launch a clean 1.21.1 Fabric profile with only Fabric API. If that works, add mods back one at a time.

6. Review your memory setting

Too little memory can crash heavy mod setups, and a huge value can also cause trouble on low-RAM PCs. Around 4 GB is a safe starting point for most Fabric setups. See the RAM guide.

7. Update your graphics driver

Crashes on startup that mention graphics or OpenGL are often fixed by updating your GPU driver from the manufacturer.

8. Read the crash report

Minecraft writes a crash report when it fails. In the standard setup it is saved in the crash-reports folder inside your game folder. Look near the top for the mod name and for lines starting with "Caused by".

Ask for help the safe way

Share only the relevant part of the report in the FireClient Discord. Never post account files, access tokens or unredacted logs that contain personal paths.

item.title: Minecraft Java vs Bedrock: which edition should you play?
item.description: Java or Bedrock? Compare platforms, mods, servers and cross-play, learn how to check which edition you own, and see which one FireClient supports.
item.content:encoded:
Minecraft comes in two main versions for most players: Java Edition and Bedrock Edition. They share the same core game but differ in platforms, mods, servers and how you launch them. Here is a plain comparison so you can pick the one that fits.

Quick comparison

  • Platforms. Java runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. Bedrock runs on Windows, consoles, phones and tablets.
  • Mods. Java has a large mod scene through loaders such as Fabric and Forge. Bedrock uses add-ons and Marketplace content instead of mods.
  • Servers. Java has a huge community-server scene, including servers built on Paper. Bedrock has its own server ecosystem and featured servers.
  • Cross-play. Bedrock players can usually play with friends across consoles, phones and PC. Java players play with other Java players.
  • Launcher. Java starts from a launcher, which is where tools such as FireClient come in. Bedrock on Windows starts from its own app.

How to tell which one you own

Java Edition starts from the Minecraft Launcher and shows a Java Edition title. Bedrock Edition on Windows starts from the Microsoft Store app. If you bought the PC version, check your Microsoft account, because the PC purchase often includes both editions.

Which should you pick?

Pick Java if you want mods, custom launchers, the classic server scene or a customisable HUD. Pick Bedrock if you play on a console or phone, or want cross-play with friends on other devices. You can own both and switch.

Where FireClient fits

FireClient is for Java Edition on Windows 10 and 11. It does not run on Bedrock, MCPE, phones, consoles, macOS or Linux, as explained in the Bedrock and MCPE guide. If you play Java on a Windows PC, start with the install guide.

item.title: Free Minecraft launcher for Windows: what to look for
item.description: What makes a good free Minecraft Java launcher for Windows: safe downloads, mod support, memory control, worlds management and honest limits, and where FireClient fits.
item.content:encoded:
There is no single best Minecraft launcher for everyone. The right one depends on your version, your mods and how much you care about a clean setup. Use this checklist to compare any launcher, including ours.

1. A trustworthy download

Look for an official site, a public release page and a published checksum. Be careful with launchers shared through video descriptions or reupload sites. Our own safety guide shows how to verify an installer.

2. Real account handling

A launcher should let you sign in with your own Microsoft account for online play, and should be clear about what it stores. Avoid anything that asks you to paste access tokens.

3. Mod and version management

Check whether it supports the loader you use (Fabric, Forge and others), whether it can browse Modrinth, and whether it keeps separate profiles so one broken mod does not ruin everything.

4. Memory and performance controls

You should be able to set the memory budget without editing command lines. See the RAM guide for sensible numbers.

5. Worlds, resource packs and backups

A good launcher shows your worlds and helps you keep them safe when you update or uninstall.

6. Honest limits

Read what the project says it cannot do yet. Marketing that promises everything is a warning sign.

Where FireClient fits

FireClient is a free launcher for Minecraft Java Edition on Windows 10 and 11, with a Fabric in-game client for 1.21.1. It has a draggable HUD with 11 elements, 3 accent themes, a Modrinth mod manager, a worlds library, a memory setting, local skins and Paper server hosting.

It is also early access. The installer is unsigned, the in-game mod covers Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric only, and the crosshair editor and cosmetics are planned but not built. The full version is planned for November 2026 with no exact date yet. If that suits you, the download page has the installer, or read the early access details first.

item.title: How to install Fabric mods for Minecraft 1.21.1 from Modrinth
item.description: Install Fabric mods for Minecraft 1.21.1 from Modrinth: check the version and loader, add Fabric API, test one mod at a time, and use the FireClient mod manager.
item.content:encoded:
Mods for Minecraft 1.21.1 only work if they match your game version and mod loader. This guide covers the checks that prevent most crashes, and how the FireClient mod manager fits in.

What you need

  • Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.1
  • The Fabric loader for 1.21.1
  • Fabric API, which many mods require

Pick the right file on Modrinth

On a mod page at Modrinth, open the Versions tab and filter by 1.21.1 and Fabric. A file for another Minecraft version or another loader (Forge, NeoForge, Quilt) will not load on your setup. Read the dependencies list on the page and install anything marked required.

Install with the FireClient mod manager

The FireClient launcher has a mods page with Modrinth browsing, your own jar files, and curated packs for Performance, Visuals, Utility and PvP. Use it to add mods to your Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric profile so the files land in the right folder. Make sure the profile is set to 1.21.1 Fabric before you add anything. See the install guide if you have not set up the launcher yet.

Install one at a time

Add one mod, launch the game, and check that it opens. Then add the next. When something crashes, you know which mod caused it. Installing twenty at once and guessing is the slow way.

Fix a crash

  • Remove the last mod you added and start again
  • Check that every mod lists 1.21.1 and Fabric, and that Fabric API is present
  • Read the crash report for the mod name near the top, and look for a missing dependency
  • Ask in the FireClient Discord and share only the relevant part of the log, never account files or tokens

Protect your worlds

Mods can change how a world is saved. Make a copy of important worlds before you try a large new set of mods. For better frames, pair this with the FPS guide.

item.title: How to boost FPS in Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric
item.description: Raise Minecraft 1.21.1 FPS on Fabric: lower render distance, set sensible RAM, use well-known Fabric performance mods from Modrinth, and measure with an FPS HUD.
item.content:encoded:
Low FPS in Minecraft 1.21.1 usually comes from a few causes you can fix: view distance, memory, background apps and missing optimisation mods. Work through the list below, changing one thing at a time so you can see what helped.

1. Measure first

Turn on the FPS element on your FireClient HUD and play the same world for a few minutes before you change anything. Write the number down. Without a baseline you cannot tell what worked.

2. Lower the distance settings

Render distance and simulation distance have the biggest effect on most PCs. Try 10 to 12 chunks for render distance, and 6 to 8 for simulation distance, then raise them if you have headroom. Fancy graphics, smooth lighting and high particle settings cost frames too.

3. Set sensible memory

More RAM is not always faster. For Fabric with performance mods, around 4 GB is a comfortable start. Our RAM guide explains how to pick a number and where to set it in the launcher.

4. Use Java 21

Minecraft 1.21.1 runs on Java 21. An old Java runtime can cause slower performance or refuse to start the game at all.

5. Add performance mods from Modrinth

Fabric has well-known optimisation mods on Modrinth, including Sodium for rendering, Lithium for game logic and FerriteCore for memory use. Always open the mod page and check that it lists Minecraft 1.21.1 and Fabric before you install it. The FireClient launcher has a mod manager with Modrinth support and a curated Performance pack. The mods guide shows the steps.

6. Close what you do not need

Browsers with many tabs, screen recorders and overlays compete for memory and GPU time. Close them while you test, and make sure your laptop is plugged in and not on a battery saver plan.

7. Compare and keep what works

Check your FPS number again after each change. If something made no difference or caused crashes, undo it. Results depend heavily on your CPU, GPU and the mods you run, so treat the numbers here as a starting point, not a promise.

item.title: Does FireClient work on Minecraft Bedrock, MCPE or mobile?
item.description: FireClient is for Minecraft Java Edition on Windows 10 and 11. It does not run on Bedrock, MCPE, phones, consoles, macOS or Linux. Here is how to check your edition.
item.content:encoded:
Short answer: no. FireClient is a launcher and Fabric client for Minecraft Java Edition on Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit). It does not work with Minecraft Bedrock Edition, Minecraft Pocket Edition (MCPE), Minecraft on phones or tablets, or consoles.

What FireClient supports today

  • Minecraft Java Edition on Windows 10 and 11
  • The in-game client (HUD and menu) for Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric with Java 21
  • Other Java versions can be launched, but they run without the FireClient mod

What it does not support

  • Bedrock Edition on Windows, Xbox, PlayStation or Switch
  • MCPE and Minecraft on Android or iOS
  • macOS and Linux (the launcher is Windows only for now)

How to tell which edition you own

Java Edition starts from the Minecraft Launcher and has a "Java" title. Bedrock Edition on Windows starts from the Microsoft Store app. If you bought Minecraft for Windows from the Microsoft Store as a single "Bedrock" game, check your Microsoft account for Java Edition as well, because many accounts include both.

Where to go next

If you play Java Edition on a Windows PC, start with the install guide or the download page. For Bedrock or mobile, you need a different tool. We would rather say so than send you to an installer that will not work for you. Current limits are listed on the early access page.

item.title: Is FireClient safe? How to check your download
item.description: Is FireClient safe to install? Where the official download lives, why the beta installer is unsigned, and how to check its SHA-256 before you run it.
item.content:encoded:
People search "is FireClient safe" for a good reason: any Minecraft client installer deserves a second look before you run it. This page tells you exactly where the official download lives, what is unusual about the current build, and how to check your file yourself. It is not a guarantee, and you should make the call with the facts.

Official sources only

Download FireClient from fireclient.net or from the official GitHub Releases page. If a file comes from a video description, a random mirror or a Discord direct message, do not run it. Links on this site point to the GitHub release file.

Why Windows may show a warning

The current early access installer is unsigned. We do not have a paid code-signing certificate yet, so Windows SmartScreen can show a prompt for an app it does not recognise. That prompt is expected for a new unsigned installer. It does not prove the file is safe, and it does not prove it is unsafe. It means Windows has no reputation data for it yet.

Check the SHA-256 yourself

A hash is a fingerprint of a file. If your copy has the same SHA-256 as the one published on the download page, the file was not changed on the way to you. In PowerShell:

Get-FileHash .\FireClient-Setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256

Compare the result with the hash shown on the download page. If they differ, delete the file and download it again from an official source.

Good habits for any Minecraft client

  • Never paste your Microsoft or Minecraft access token, account files or unredacted logs into a public chat
  • Read what the app asks permission for, and read the Terms and Privacy notice
  • Keep a backup of worlds you care about before changing game files
  • Scan the file with Windows Security or your own antivirus if you want another opinion

What FireClient needs from you

To play online you need your own Minecraft Java Edition account. FireClient does not give you the game for free. See the install guide for the full steps, and ask in the Discord if something looks wrong.

item.title: How much RAM should you give Minecraft? A practical guide
item.description: How much RAM to give Minecraft: sensible starting points for vanilla, Fabric performance mods and big modpacks, plus how to set memory in FireClient.
item.content:encoded:
Giving Minecraft more memory does not always make it faster. Too little causes stutters and crashes. Too much can make garbage collection pauses longer and starves the rest of your PC. This guide gives sensible starting points and shows where the setting lives in FireClient.

Quick starting points

These are rules of thumb, not guarantees. Mods, shaders and view distance change the picture.

  • Vanilla Minecraft 1.21: 2 to 4 GB is usually enough
  • Performance mods on Fabric: 4 GB is a comfortable start
  • Large modpacks or heavy shaders: 6 to 8 GB, raised only if you actually run out

Do not give it everything

Leave at least 2 to 4 GB for Windows and your other apps. If your PC has 8 GB in total, 4 GB for Minecraft is a sensible ceiling. Asking for more than your system can spare pushes memory onto the disk, which is slower than a smaller allocation.

Set it in FireClient

In the launcher settings, choose a memory budget. FireClient passes it to Java as the maximum heap and limits it to a safe range, so an extreme value cannot be set by mistake.

Signs you need more, or less

  • Crashes with an out-of-memory error, or stutters that get worse over time: raise it by 1 GB and test again
  • Short freezes every few seconds on a high setting: try lowering it
  • Slow loading while other apps compete for memory: close them or reduce the amount

Check your result

Change one thing at a time. Keep the FPS and Memory elements on your FireClient HUD while you play for ten minutes, then compare. If you are new to the launcher, start with the install guide.

item.title: Back up and reuse your FireClient HUD layout
item.description: Back up your FireClient HUD layout by copying client.json, and move your HUD setup to another PC. Includes how to fix elements that end up off screen.
item.content:encoded:
Your HUD layout takes a few minutes to set up, so it is worth backing up. FireClient keeps it in one small file.

Where the layout is stored

Positions, visibility and the sprint toggle are saved to config/fireclient/client.json. The path is relative to your Minecraft game folder, so look for a config folder inside it, then fireclient.

Back it up

  1. Close Minecraft so the file is not being written.
  2. Copy client.json to a safe place, such as a cloud folder or a USB drive.
  3. Put a date in the copy's name, for example client-2026-10-13.json, so you can keep a few versions.

Reuse it on another PC

Install FireClient on the other PC and run Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric once, so the config/fireclient folder exists. Close the game, then put your copy in that folder as client.json. The layout should load the next time you start the game. Keep a copy of the original first in case you want to go back.

When something looks wrong

If elements end up off screen after a resolution change, open the menu with Right Shift and use Edit HUD Positions to drag them back. The HUD setup guide has the full walkthrough.

Before you share the file

The file holds layout settings, but open it in a text editor and check it before you post it anywhere. Never post logs or account files publicly. If you are unsure, ask in the FireClient Discord.

item.title: How to set up the FireClient HUD in Minecraft 1.21.1
item.description: Set up the FireClient HUD in Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric: open the menu with Right Shift, toggle FPS, CPS and keystrokes, and drag each element into place.
item.content:encoded:
FireClient adds a HUD and an in-game menu to Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric. This guide covers how to open the menu, turn elements on, move them, and where your layout is saved.

Open the menu

Start a Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric world and press Right Shift. You can also use the FireClient Menu button on the title screen. The menu has four tabs: HUD, Features, Theme and About.

Choose your HUD elements

The HUD tab has a switch for each element. FireClient includes eleven:

  • Watermark
  • FPS
  • Coordinates
  • Ping
  • Direction
  • Memory
  • Clock
  • Keystrokes
  • Armor
  • Effects
  • CPS

Turn on only what you read during play. A short list keeps the screen clear, whether you are in a PvP match or building.

Move things with the HUD editor

Press Edit HUD Positions and drag each element where you want it. Positions, visibility and the sprint toggle are saved to config/fireclient/client.json, so your layout is the same the next time you launch.

Pick an accent theme

The Theme tab has three accent themes. You can switch at any time, and the change shows up in the menu and HUD right away.

What you need

The in-game client is built for Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric with Java 21. The launcher can start other versions, but they launch without the FireClient mod.

Questions? Ask in the FireClient Discord, or download FireClient to try the HUD yourself.

item.title: Install FireClient on Windows in five steps
item.description: Install the FireClient Minecraft launcher on Windows 10 or 11: download, verify the SHA-256, run the unsigned installer, sign in and play 1.21.1 Fabric.
item.content:encoded:
FireClient is a free launcher and Fabric client for Minecraft Java Edition on Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit). The installer sets up the launcher; you need your own Minecraft Java Edition account to play online.

1. Download the installer

Get the installer from the Download section. Wait for the file to finish before you open it.

2. Verify the SHA-256 (optional)

The current beta installer is unsigned, so Windows may show a security prompt. To check that your file is the one we published, compare its hash with the SHA-256 on the download page. In PowerShell:

Get-FileHash .\FireClient-Setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256

3. Run the installer

Accept the terms and allow the Windows prompt if you trust the source. Read the Terms and Privacy notice first if you have not.

4. Sign in

Sign in with Microsoft, or use an offline profile.

5. Play 1.21.1 Fabric

Launch Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric to get the in-game menu on Right Shift. The HUD setup guide shows what to do next.

Will an update delete my worlds?

No. The installer and uninstaller leave your game-data folder in place, including worlds and resource packs. Back up important worlds before you change game files anyway.

item.title: FireClient 1.0 is available as a free Windows beta
item.description: FireClient 1.0 is a free Windows beta: a Minecraft Java launcher with a Fabric 1.21.1 in-game client, mod manager, worlds library and draggable HUD.
item.content:encoded:
FireClient 1.0 is available as a free beta for Windows 10 and 11. It pairs a launcher for Minecraft Java Edition with a Fabric in-game client for Minecraft 1.21.1.

What is in 1.0

  • The launcher memory setting is passed to Java as the max heap, limited to a safe range.
  • The saves library shows each world's own icon, last-saved date and size.
  • The resource pack library has no delete action. Packs and worlds stay on disk through updates and uninstall.
  • The in-game client has a draggable HUD with eleven elements and three accent themes.

Known issues

  • The installer is unsigned, so Windows may show a security prompt.
  • The in-game mod is built for Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric only. Other versions launch without it.

Planned

A crosshair editor and cosmetics are planned but not built yet.

Download FireClient or read the installation guide. Feedback and bug reports are welcome in the Discord.
